title: Backend mid scenario deadlock incident
question: Your database logs show periodic deadlock errors between two transactions, and some requests are failing as a result. How do you investigate and fix it?
idealAnswer:
Identifies the root cause pattern: two transactions acquiring the same two locks in opposite orders is the classic recipe for a deadlock, the database detects the cycle and kills one transaction to break it

Would pull the actual deadlock log/trace to confirm which tables and rows were involved rather than guessing

Proposes the standard fix: enforce a consistent lock acquisition order across all code paths (e.g. always touch accounts before transfers, everywhere), which eliminates the possibility of a cycle

Mentions handling the immediate symptom too, the losing transaction should be retried by the application (deadlocks are expected to happen occasionally even with good ordering, under real concurrency), not just left to fail

Considers keeping transactions short and touching as few rows as possible to reduce the window where a deadlock can occur, in addition to fixing the ordering
